newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Mobil Nigeria denies sacking 2,000 workers.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Nigeria denies sacking 2,000 workers.

text.p: Mobil Producing Nigeria Unlimited on Wednesday denied it had sacked 2,000 workers.

The company, a joint venture with state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp was responding to a local newspaper report quoting its out-going managing director, Jim Massey as saying the workers were sacked because a cut-back on its 1997 operating budget by the Nigerian government.
"At no time did Mr Massey say that we had laid off or were planning to lay off any of our employees," Mobil said in a statement.

According to the statement, Massey only said that the budget cut-back "has necessitated the release of three rigs working in the NNPC/Mobil joint concessions which does not in any way imply that Mobil Producing Nigeria had sacked any of its employees."
The rigs are operated under contract agreements by oil service companies.

Mobil Producing said it had a workfoce of 1,500 personnel and had no intention to reduce it and that it was still committed to achieving a daily production target of 900,000 barrels by the turn of the century.
It currently pumps about half that target.
